completedSteps: Added infra/v3/backup.sh: a daily host-native backup (same pattern as CS-24's monitor.sh - runs on the host, not in a container). Every run: (1) pg_dump via docker exec, custom format, captured to a staging file on the host; (2) restores that exact dump into a disposable scratch database inside the same container and runs a real sanity query (table count), then drops the scratch DB - this is what makes the restore exercised, not documented (AC2), since every scheduled run proves its own dump is actually restorable, not just that pg_dump exited zero; (3) only if both succeed, atomically renames the verified dump into place (root-only 0600) and applies retention (default 14 days). Any failure at any step deletes the bad attempt, leaves the last good file byte-identical and untouched, records STATUS=failed with a reason in a status file, and alerts a webhook - so a failed dump can never look like a current one (AC3).

Added careerscope-backup.service/.timer (daily at 03:30, RandomizedDelaySec, Persistent) and setup-backup.sh (idempotent installer, mirrors setup-monitoring.sh: root-only 0600 /etc/careerscope-backup.env, 0700 backup dir, runs one real backup immediately on install). Added infra/v3/check-backup.sh: unlike check-monitoring.sh this is NOT stub-based - it starts a real disposable postgres:17.6-alpine container, seeds real tables/rows, and runs the actual pg_dump/pg_restore/sanity-query pipeline end to end, because AC2 specifically demands the restore be proven with a real database, not simulated. 17/19 automated checks pass; the remaining 2 (dump/dir permission bits reporting 644/755 instead of 600/700) were independently proven, via a bare chmod+stat round-trip with zero backup.sh code involved, to be a Git-Bash-on-Windows/NTFS permission-reporting limitation of this local dev environment, not a defect - confirmed twice, once by me and once independently by QA. Wired into CI (ci.yml verify job, which runs on real Linux where these checks are meaningful).

Added docs/OPERATIONS/BACKUP.md (design, install, how to actually restore a real dump, verification) and a one-time manual-install step in docs/OPERATIONS/DEPLOYMENT.md. Added a KNOWN-LIMITATIONS note extending CS-24's 'nothing watches the watcher' entry to cover careerscope-backup.timer for the same reason.

Real Security review (native runSubagent): APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. One real P2, fixed: the documented webhook fallback (BACKUP_WEBHOOK_URL falling back to MONITOR_WEBHOOK_URL) was never actually reachable - systemd's EnvironmentFile only loads the file(s) named in the unit, and careerscope-backup.service only named its own env file, so an operator who set up CS-24's webhook and trusted the documented CS-25 fallback would get silent backup-failure alerts. Fixed by loading /etc/careerscope-monitor.env before /etc/careerscope-backup.env in the service unit. Two P3s fixed: BACKUP_VERIFY_DB is now validated against a plain-identifier pattern before being interpolated into SQL (removes the assumption that only root can ever set it, rather than resting on it); a manual run overlapping the timer's own run could race for the same scratch database (never unsafe - confirmed no path silently reuses a data-contaminated leftover - but wasteful, discarding a good dump and firing a spurious failure alert) - fixed with a best-effort flock (skips locking gracefully if flock isn't installed, rather than turning a missing tool into a backup outage). Confirmed: no permission TOCTOU (directory chmod happens before any data exists), no command injection at the argv level, no private dump content ever reaches a log or alert message, retention's -mtime argument can't be injection-attacked, and the webhook-alerting code is byte-for-byte the same proven pattern as CS-24's monitor.sh, not a weaker reimplementation.

Traced the full file and confirmed there is exactly one promote line (mv -f) and every gate above it routes through fail() first. Proved the guard is non-vacuous with a live mutation test on a scratch copy: neutralized fail()'s early-exit, ran the (also-scratch-copied) test suite against the broken script, watched 8 checks fail including the specific promotion-guard assertion, discarded every scratch artifact, and re-confirmed the real unmodified files still pass 17/19. Confirmed setup-backup.sh/service/timer path consistency, confirmed the webhook code matches monitor.sh's exactly, confirmed npm run format:check is clean for both new docs, confirmed no leftover Docker containers after the real test run.
